claims.text: IDSA treatment courses for oral thrush last 7 to 14 days
claims.quote: For mild disease, clotrimazole troches, 10 mg 5 times daily, OR miconazole mucoadhesive buccal 50 mg tablet applied to the mucosal surface over the canine fossa once daily for 7-14 days, are recommended

claims.text: Mild disease: clotrimazole troches or miconazole buccal tablet; nystatin suspension 4-6 mL four times daily is an alternative; 7 to 14 days
claims.quote: Alternatives for mild disease include nystatin suspension (100 000 U/mL) 4-6 mL 4 times daily, OR 1-2 nystatin pastilles (200 000 U each) 4 times daily, for 7-14 days

claims.text: Moderate to severe disease: oral fluconazole 100-200 mg daily for 7 to 14 days (local treatment for mild disease, so a pill is not automatically better)
claims.quote: For moderate to severe disease, oral fluconazole, 100-200 mg daily, for 7-14 days is recommended (strong recommendation; high-quality evidence).

claims.text: Risk factors include antibiotics, steroids, dentures, diabetes, HIV, cancer; thrush is a recognized indicator of immune dysfunction
claims.quote: Oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis occur in association with HIV infection, diabetes, leukemia and other malignancies, steroid use, radiation therapy, antimicrobial therapy, and denture use [528,529], and their occurrence is recognized as an indicator of immune dysfunction.

claims.text: For denture-related thrush, disinfect dentures alongside antifungal treatment
claims.quote: For denture-related candidiasis, disinfection of the denture, in addition to antifungal therapy, is recommended (strong recommendation; moderate-quality evidence).

claims.text: Painful swallowing can mean esophageal involvement; esophageal candidiasis can occur without obvious mouth thrush
claims.quote: esophageal candidiasis can present as odynophagia without concomitant oropharyngeal candidiasis.

claims.text: Esophageal candidiasis: systemic antifungal therapy is always required
claims.quote: What Is the Treatment for Esophageal Candidiasis? Recommendations 131. Systemic antifungal therapy is always required.

claims.text: Recurrent infections typically occur with persistent immunosuppression; recurrence warrants review rather than automatic repeat antifungals
claims.quote: Recurrent infections typically occur in patients who have persistent immunosuppression, especially those who have AIDS and low CD4 cell counts (<50 cells/µL)

claims.text: Repeated azoles without review are not the default for recurrence
claims.quote: Chronic suppressive therapy is usually unnecessary. If required for patients who have recurrent infection, fluconazole, 100 mg 3 times weekly, is recommended

claims.text: Infection that does not respond to fluconazole (refractory disease) is a recognized cause of persistence
claims.quote: For fluconazole-refractory disease, itraconazole solution, 200 mg once daily OR posaconazole suspension, 400 mg twice daily for 3 days then 400 mg daily, for up to 28 days, are recommended

claims.text: Much of the trial evidence comes from people with HIV
claims.quote: In a multicenter randomized study among HIVinfected individuals, 50-mg mucoadhesive buccal tablets of miconazole applied once daily to the mucosal surface over the canine fossa were as effective as 10-mg clotrimazole troches used 5 times daily

claims.text: Candida cleanse diets are not among IDSA-recommended treatments, which are antifungal medicines
claims.quote: For mild disease, clotrimazole troches, 10 mg 5 times daily, OR miconazole mucoadhesive buccal 50 mg tablet applied to the mucosal surface over the canine fossa once daily for 7-14 days, are recommended

claims.text: Common regimens per table: clotrimazole 5 times daily 7-14 days; nystatin 4-6 mL four times daily 7-14 days; fluconazole 100-200 mg daily 7-14 days
claims.quote: For moderate to severe disease, oral fluconazole, 100-200 mg daily, for 7-14 days is recommended (strong recommendation; high-quality evidence).
